oil.summary: WTI and Brent surged roughly 5.3-5.4% on the day, recovering sharply from a brutal month that has erased more than 20% from both benchmarks. The catalyst was a clear geopolitical shock: drone strikes in the Strait of Hormuz disrupted shipping, and the US subsequently revoked Iran's oil sanctions waiver in direct response to tanker attacks, ratcheting up pressure on Tehran. Ukraine compounded supply-side anxiety by striking Russia's largest refinery and a Kerch terminal in Crimea. Against that backdrop, the UAE's post-OPEC output surge to above 3.8 mb/d and an API crude draw of only 399,000 barrels for the week ending July 3 offered mixed signals on fundamentals. RBOB gasoline bucked the crude rally, falling 5.6% on the day, suggesting crack-spread compression rather than demand strength. Saudi Arabia's reported plans to expand its East-West pipeline capacity by up to 2 mb/d signal Riyadh is preparing longer-term Hormuz bypass optionality.
drivers: US revocation of Iran oil sanctions waiver following Hormuz tanker drone attacks drove a sharp geopolitical risk premium into crude prices
Ukraine struck Russia's largest oil refinery and Kerch terminal in Crimea, adding further supply disruption concerns
UAE raised output to above 3.8 mb/d after quitting OPEC, while API data showed a modest US crude stock draw of 399,000 barrels, keeping fundamental picture mixed

gas.summary: European TTF jumped 4.96% on the day to 46.32 €/MWh, extending a strong weekly gain of 8.82% that likely reflects spillover from Hormuz supply-risk anxiety and broader energy security concerns. Henry Hub was more subdued, adding 1.11% to $3.281/MMBtu, still up over 3% on the week. On the structural side, ADNOC signed a 15-year LNG supply agreement with Japan's Inpex for volumes from the Ruwais LNG project, underscoring ongoing Asian demand for long-term contracted LNG. Germany announced a $1.7 billion plan to create a state-owned strategic natural gas reserve, signalling continued European appetite for supply security buffers. A headline noting Chevron and Exxon are expected to report their best quarter since 2022 points to the supportive revenue environment for gas-weighted majors.
drivers: TTF surged nearly 5% on the day, likely driven by Hormuz geopolitical risk spilling into European gas supply anxiety
Germany announced a $1.7 billion state-owned strategic natural gas reserve, reinforcing European energy security demand
ADNOC signed a 15-year LNG supply deal with Japan's Inpex for Ruwais LNG volumes, highlighting durable long-term Asian LNG contracting appetite

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs slipped 1.99% on the day to $75.985/EUA, a modest pullback that sits against a still-positive one-month gain of 4.28%. The softness in EUAs despite a sharp TTF rally is notable; higher gas prices would normally lift carbon as coal-to-gas switching dynamics tighten. Headline flow for the power and carbon space is thin today beyond the Hormuz and Ukraine drone-strike themes that pervade all three sectors. A drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant — reported on July 6 — added a nuclear supply-risk dimension. Trump's nuclear loan programme drew commentary that it fails to address deeper structural issues in the US power market even as AI-driven electricity demand accelerates. Direct power-market price data beyond TTF and EUAs was not available in today's feed.
drivers: EUA prices dipped ~2% despite a nearly 5% TTF rally, suggesting carbon-specific selling pressure overrode the usual gas-price correlation
Drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant introduced a new dimension of generation-asset geopolitical risk
Trump's nuclear loan programme is under scrutiny for failing to address structural US power market gaps as AI-driven load growth accelerates
